Definition: from G1223 and G3739; through which thing, i.e. consequently:--for which cause, therefore, wherefore.
BiblicalUsage: Therefore, the small word that turns a truth into a command. Paul argues from what God has done to what we must do, and Peter does the same when he tells us to gird up our minds because Christ is coming. The therefore always points backward before it points forward.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Christian life runs on therefores. Because God has done this, I do that, and whenever I lose the reason, the obedience loses its strength, so I keep going back to what God has done.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
